grants.funder: Stigler Center, University of Chicago Booth School of Business
grants.summary: A twelve-week residence on the Chicago Hyde Park campus for working journalists with an interest in political economy. The centre covers living costs, airfare, visa fees and health insurance, so the fellow is not funding the stay themselves.

amount.note: $14,000 towards living expenses over twelve weeks, plus economy airfare to and from Chicago, SEVIS and visa fees, and health insurance. Fellows need their own funds for roughly the first month, before the stipend is paid.

grants.notes: Residence runs tentatively 15 March – 31 May 2027. Applicants need professional journalism experience, proficient English and an interest in political economy. Read on the centre's own page: deadline "September 20, 2026 by 11:59 p.m. CT Chicago time".

pinned._why: Added by hand after a reader noticed it was missing. Verified on the centre's own page on 18 September 2026, two days before it closes — too close to the deadline to risk the sweep re-reading it wrongly.

grants.summary: Project grants for cross-border cooperation involving Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia; Visegrad+ extends eligibility to the Western Balkans and Eastern Partnership. Media and journalism projects are eligible.
grants.notes: Not yet verified. The fund historically ran fixed deadlines several times a year — confirm the current calendar.

grants.summary: Membership programme covering legal costs of defending public-interest reporting against defamation and similar suits, aimed at small and mid-sized outlets and independent journalists.

amount.note: Cover rather than cash; membership fees apply

grants.notes: Not yet verified against the programme's site.

grants.funder: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, Oxford
grants.summary: Term-length fellowships at Oxford for working journalists to research a topic of their choice, with some funded places available.

amount.note: Funded and self-funded places

grants.notes: Not yet verified against the institute's site.

grants.funder: CERC Migration and Integration / Toronto Metropolitan University
grants.summary: A one-month residency at Toronto Metropolitan University for a journalist to engage with migration research and develop reporting informed by that scholarship. Includes a stipend covering the residency period and travel.

amount.note: Total stipend value of CAD 5,000 including a travel allowance.

grants.notes: IJNet's opportunities page did not render usable content in today's snapshot (JS-rendered, only nav captured). grants.funder: Reynolds Center for Business Journalism, Cronkite School (ASU)
grants.programme: James B. Steele Fellowship in Investigative Business Journalism
grants.summary: A one-year fellowship combining a master's degree, mentored investigative reporting projects, and an internship at a major media organization, aimed at early-career business journalists.

amount.note: Covers tuition, a stipend, and health insurance; exact stipend amount not stated.

grants.notes: IJNet's opportunities page did not render usable content in today's snapshot. Deadline reconfirmed via the funder's own businessjournalism.org site (Jan 1, 2027). Not confirmed on the funder's own page in this session.

grants.summary: Grants for journalists, media professionals and organizations advocating for press freedom, newsroom resilience, media literacy and public trust in journalism; a separate small Freelance Fund mini-grant also exists for SPJ members.

amount.note: Main grant-cycle amounts not stated; a separate Freelance Fund mini-grant tops out at $500 and requires paid SPJ membership.

grants.notes: Primarily US-focused (SPJ is a US organization). Deadline already passed; annual recurring cycle. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A long-running programme supporting cross-border teams of professional journalists and/or news outlets investigating European topics, across several application rounds per year.

amount.note: €280,000 total pool distributed per call round among all funded projects; individual award size not stated.

grants.notes: Teams of at least 2 professional journalists/outlets from at least 2 different European countries; at least 80% of budget must go to EU-based team members. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Grants for cross-border teams investigating environmental issues, funding reporting costs for print, online, or broadcast stories with a strong environmental angle related to Europe. Supported investigations must result in publications in at least two media outlets in different countries.

amount.note: €400,000 available per call; individual grant amount not stated.

grants.notes: Last confirmed 2026 round closed 6 Aug 2026; no next round date has been announced yet on the funder's site or its grants portal. Solo applications are not eligible — must be a team of at least two journalists/outlets from different countries.

grants.summary: Grants of €5,000-€50,000, covering up to 100% of project costs, for cross-border investigative journalism teams of any kind (freelance, staff or mixed) working across eligible European countries. Currently paused between rounds; the next call opens 1 December 2026.

amount.note: €1.2 million total available across the 2026-27 funding cycle.

grants.notes: Deadline for each call is nine weeks from its launch date; the exact date is not yet set for the round opening 1 December 2026. Managed by the International Press Institute.

grants.summary: Grants of up to €20,000 plus mentoring, training and networking support for cross-border teams of at least two freelance journalists based in different eligible European countries. The scheme is currently paused between rounds; the next call opens 1 December 2026.

amount.note: Around €400,000 in total grants planned across the 2026-27 funding round.

grants.notes: Deadline for each call is nine weeks from its launch date; the exact date is not yet set for the round opening 1 December 2026. Managed by the European Journalism Centre.

grants.programme: Travel grant to attend IJ4EU UNCOVERED 2026
grants.summary: Small travel grants to help journalists attend the IJ4EU UNCOVERED conference, a networking and training event for investigative journalists in Europe.
grants.notes: This is a conference-attendance travel grant, not a reporting grant. Deadline already passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Rolling-basis grants supporting in-depth, high-impact reporting on underreported global issues, open to journalists and newsrooms worldwide with no restriction on topic or reporting location. This is the Pulitzer Center's signature, catch-all reporting grant.

amount.note: Typically $5,000-$10,000 for international travel costs; larger amounts considered in exceptional cases.

grants.notes: Accepted year-round with no fixed deadline; reconfirmed as still listed on today's snapshot. Amount figure sourced via web search. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Supports print, broadcast, digital and multimedia investigative reporting on the forces driving racism, antisemitism, Islamophobia, misogyny and other forms of intolerance and hate within the United States.

amount.note: Grants range from $2,500 to $10,000.

grants.notes: Three-year programme funding staff and freelance journalists' US-based reporting.

grants.programme: Kari Howard Fund for Narrative Journalism (2026)
grants.summary: Supports narrative (long-form) journalism projects by women and nonbinary journalists, funding reporting and production costs for stories published in English.

amount.note: Grants reported as averaging about $5,000.

grants.notes: Open to women and nonbinary journalists (freelance or staff); reporting and publication must be in English. 2026 window (closed July 12) has ended; next cycle timing unknown. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A fellowship providing academic and professional opportunities at MIT and internships at The Boston Globe and The New York Times for women and nonbinary journalists focused on human rights and social justice, with at least three years' professional experience.
grants.notes: Page states: 'Applications for the 2027 Elizabeth Neuffer Fellowship are now closed. All applicants will receive an update on their application by end-July 2026.' No new deadline announced.

grants.summary: FIJ's core grant programme supports U.S. and international investigative reporting projects across print, online, broadcast, books, documentaries and podcasts. Grants of up to $10,000 are reviewed three to four times a year and can cover reporting time and out-of-pocket costs such as travel, records requests and equipment.

amount.note: Maximum grant is $10,000; covers reporting time plus out-of-pocket expenses such as travel, document collection and equipment rental.

grants.notes: FIJ's 2026 deadlines (Jan 30, Apr 27, Sep 14) have passed; the next stated deadline is Friday, January 29, 2027. A separate rolling track exists for applicants who previously received FIJ Seed funding (decisions in 2-4 weeks); not broken out separately here.

grants.summary: Small grants of up to $2,500 for preliminary investigative reporting, such as open-records requests and initial reporting trips, intended to lead to a full investigation. Applications are reviewed a couple of times a year.
grants.notes: FIJ's own page gives conflicting next-deadline statements for Seed Funding: 'Friday, January 29, 2027' in one section and 'Friday, May 10' (no year given, under a stale '2026 Grant Application Deadlines' heading) in another. Deadline left blank rather than guessing which is correct.

grants.funder: Fund for Investigative Journalism (FIJ) / Alicia Patterson Foundation
grants.summary: A fellowship supporting a single in-depth, long-form investigative reporting and writing project over six or twelve months. The Alicia Patterson Foundation merged into FIJ in December 2025.

amount.note: Up to $20,000 for a 6-month fellowship, or up to $40,000 for a 12-month fellowship.

grants.notes: Deadline confirmed verbatim on FIJ's own page today ('The next deadline is Thursday, October 1, 2026').

grants.summary: Reporting grants to produce in-depth, published journalism on biodiversity and nature-based solutions, paired with editorial mentorship, for journalists in Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya, Kyrgyzstan and Madagascar.

amount.note: Up to 25 grants, average budget approximately €1,800 each.

grants.notes: No snapshot available today (source fetch failed, HTTP 403). Re-verified via search of EJN's own site; the deadline was 30 June 2026 and has passed, so status moves from 'open' to 'closed' (80 days past deadline — under the 90-day deletion threshold). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Media grants to strengthen journalism on marine conservation and countries' progress toward the global 30x30 marine target, funding newsroom reporting projects on ocean and coastal issues.

amount.note: Five grants of up to US$10,000 each — one per focus country (Ghana, Mexico, Philippines) and two open to any eligible coastal country.

grants.notes: No snapshot available today (source fetch failed, HTTP 403). Re-verified via search of EJN's own site; the deadline was 10 August 2026 (11:59 PM Asia/Manila) and has passed, so status moves from 'open' to 'closed' (39 days past deadline). Not open to individual freelancers — organisations/newsrooms only. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Emergency financial assistance for freelance journalists facing a crisis directly resulting from their work, such as physical attacks, urgent medical or equipment-replacement costs, or forced relocation.

amount.note: Assessed case-by-case.

grants.notes: Open to freelance journalists working in news and current affairs worldwide, whose sole income comes from journalism (no regular salary/retainer). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Grants for freelance journalists and their families facing financial hardship as a direct result of their journalism work, to support recovery and safer continuation of work.
grants.notes: Open to freelance journalists (and their families) worldwide, working in news and current affairs. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Bursaries covering the cost of Hostile Environment and First Aid Training (HEFAT) courses, helping freelance journalists build safety and first-aid skills for high-risk assignments.

amount.note: Covers cost of a HEFAT course.

grants.notes: Requires at least 18 months' experience in newsgathering/current affairs; priority to those working in hostile environments or with a confirmed assignment. Processing time currently around six weeks due to high volume. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A year-long remote fellowship providing a reporting grant, one-to-one mentoring, industry workshops and a peer network to help mid-career journalists and filmmakers develop existing Global South reporting.

amount.note: Up to £3,000 reporting grant.

grants.notes: Open to mid-career journalists and filmmakers based in the Global South (no single region code captures this — see summary). Call opens each February with a March deadline; 2026 Fellows already announced in June 2026, so this cycle is closed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Project grants and one-to-one mentoring for journalists reporting on under-covered climate stories, disbursed in instalments per project.

amount.note: £3,000-£5,000 per project, paid in instalments.

grants.notes: Geographic eligibility not clearly stated beyond One World Media's usual Global South focus. All funded projects were required to be completed by June 2026, so this round has ended; unclear if/when it recurs. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Grants for cross-border collaborative investigations on the impact of AI
grants.summary: Funded four grants of EUR 5,000 each to teams of journalists for cross-border collaborative investigative reporting on the impact of AI, covering a project period of September 2026 to February 2027.

amount.note: Four grants of EUR 5,000 each, to teams of journalists.

grants.notes: Open to independent European media organisations and freelance/staff journalists resident in the EU, including Ukrainian, Belarusian, or Russian journalists legally resident in the EU. Deadline has passed; kept for reference in case a future round reopens. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Practical and legal support for journalists
grants.summary: Beyond monitoring and advocacy, the MFRR consortium (led by ECPMF with ARTICLE19 Europe, EFJ, IPI, Free Press Unlimited, and OBCT) provides direct practical support to journalists in danger: medical assistance for work-related injuries, subsistence costs, psychological support, digital-safety tools, family support, and help with legal proceedings or relocation.

amount.note: No fixed amount stated; support is need-based (medical, subsistence, psychological, legal costs).

grants.notes: MFRR is primarily a monitoring/advocacy consortium, but this practical-support arm is a genuine assistance scheme delivered operationally via Free Press Unlimited's application channel. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Awards grants to nongovernmental organisations — including independent media, civic groups and associations — working to advance democratic goals, in more than 100 countries. Does not fund individuals, government bodies, or state-supported institutions.

amount.note: Described as averaging roughly USD 50,000 for a typical ~12-month grant; not a stated fixed range.

grants.notes: For organisations working in newly established democracies, semi-authoritarian states, highly repressive societies, and countries in democratic transition; generally excludes projects located in established democracies. Not open to individual freelance journalists. A quarterly submission pattern was reported but no specific 2026 date could be corroborated reliably enough to report. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: EED Open Grant / Request for Support
grants.summary: Provides flexible, rolling financial and technical support to independent media outlets, journalists, bloggers and pro-democracy civil society actors, including in repressive or conflict-affected environments.

amount.note: EED states requests for support 'usually' range €10,000-€150,000 but has no formal funding range.

grants.notes: Official registration is reportedly not required; individuals, bloggers and informal/unregistered groups are eligible alongside organisations. Rolling basis, no fixed deadline (EED aims to respond within ~12 weeks). Covers EU Eastern and Southern Neighbourhood, Western Balkans and wider region (not for EU-internal media). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Civitates (philanthropic collaborative, via King Baudouin Foundation)
grants.programme: Strengthening Independent Public Interest Journalism in Europe
grants.summary: Core funding for non-profit, independent public-interest media organisations in a set of EU countries, to strengthen organisational sustainability, business models, editorial development and audience engagement over a two-year period.

amount.note: Reported maximum of up to €160,000 per organisation over two years (~€80,000/year), capped at half the applicant's 2024 total spending.

grants.notes: Open only to media organisations registered in Hungary, Poland, Italy, Spain, Bulgaria, Slovakia and Croatia. King Baudouin Foundation has confirmed roughly €2.467M already granted to 11 outlets under this call, indicating this round has concluded; a newer 2026 round was not independently confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Recurring project grants for journalism on topics important to public debate in Norway, prioritising investigative or otherwise resource-intensive reporting. Freelancers with a publication agreement from an editorial outlet are explicitly invited to apply alongside newsrooms.

amount.note: Fritt Ord allocates up to NOK 25 million per year in total to journalism projects across all grantees; no single-grant amount was stated.

grants.notes: Freelancer applicants must submit brief verification of their publishing agreement and remuneration level; projects/topics must relate to Norwegian public debate. 2026 deadlines: Apr 24 and Aug 14 (both passed), and Oct 23 (upcoming, used here). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Fritt Ord's Journalism Fellowship at the Reuters Institute, Oxford
grants.summary: Funds a six-month fellowship at the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford, for a Norwegian journalist to conduct research and professional development abroad.
grants.notes: Open to Norwegian journalists only (fellowship hosted in Oxford, UK). Amount and current application deadline could not be confirmed via search; programme appears to run on an annual/recurring basis. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Supports individual journalists and media innovators proposing their own project targeting news innovation (new tools, formats, business models) rather than applying to a fixed call.
grants.notes: ICFJ's own page reportedly states no fixed openings are posted, but invites candidates to propose an idea for a potential fellowship at any time — treated here as a rolling, propose-based route rather than a scheduled call. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A journalist exchange programme between the US/Canada and Germany: journalists spend roughly eight weeks working in a newsroom in the partner country after a one-week orientation, to build transatlantic reporting collaboration.
grants.notes: For US/Canadian journalists, or German journalists, applying for a reciprocal exchange. The 2026 cohort's deadlines (Mar 1 for US/Canada, Feb 1 for Germany) have already passed, with the exchange running roughly late July-September 2026. Next cycle's deadlines (likely early 2027) were not found. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Expedited grants of up to $2,500 for timely follow-up coverage to an original investigation that was previously produced with FIJ grant support.
grants.notes: Open only to reporters/outlets who previously received an FIJ grant and published the resulting investigation; not a general open call.

grants.funder: European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF) — SAFE for Journalists
grants.summary: Training grants of up to €5,000 per programme for independent media outlets in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine, supporting journalist safety, digital security and organisational resilience training. Funded training must take place before 30 December 2026.

amount.note: Up to €5,000 per training programme.

grants.summary: A 12-month, part-time fellowship for journalists, researchers and policy professionals to pursue independent reporting and analysis on technology and democracy, beginning January 2027. Each fellow receives a $10,000 stipend paid quarterly.

amount.note: Paid quarterly over the 12-month fellowship.

grants.notes: Open to journalists, researchers, lawyers and policy professionals working at the intersection of technology and democracy; particularly encourages applicants from the Global Majority and underrepresented communities.

grants.funder: National Institute for Health Care Management (NIHCM) Foundation
grants.summary: Grants for U.S.-focused reporting on major health care challenges, open to journalists at news organisations, freelancers, nonprofits and universities. Individual awards typically range from $15,000-$30,000, out of a total pool of up to $460,000 for the cycle.

amount.note: Total of up to $460,000 available across the 2026-2027 cycle; most individual awards are $15,000-$30,000.

grants.notes: 2026-2027 priority topics include health care costs and quality, consolidation, AI in health care, prescription drugs, rural health, and maternal health.

grants.funder: International Press Institute (IPI) — Media Innovation Europe
grants.summary: Grants of up to €30,000 for media organisations with a developed business plan or strategy, to implement business-sustainability and innovation initiatives, plus dedicated one-to-one mentoring. No co-financing is required.

An investment vehicle (loans, equity and quasi-equity) supporting independent media companies in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia, aimed at strengthening financial sustainability and resisting media capture.

amount.note: Funding size not stated; MDIF provides loans, equity and quasi-equity investment rather than fixed grant amounts.

grants.notes: GFMD's listing title read 'LMDIF Western Balkans Fund', apparently a typographical variant of MDIF's Western Balkans Fund.

grants.funder: Henry Nxumalo Foundation, Oxpeckers, Viewfinder, IJHub, INK Centre for Investigative Journalism and Center for Collaborative Investigative Journalism (SA|AJP)
grants.programme: Southern Africa Accountability Journalism Project (SA|AJP) Investigative Journalism Grants
grants.summary: Reporting grants and editorial support for investigative stories exposing wrongdoing or accountability failures in the Southern African region. Freelancers receive input-cost support plus a flat fee per story, while selected newsrooms receive a larger grant.

amount.note: Individual freelancers: up to $300 for input costs plus a $1,200 flat fee per story (~$1,500 total); selected newsrooms: $3,000 grants (three available).

grants.notes: Focused specifically on the SADC region rather than all of Sub-Saharan Africa. Open to freelancers and to staff journalists taking a sabbatical from newsroom duties to pursue an in-depth project.

grants.summary: Grants of €25,000-€35,000 for regional cooperation projects among organisations in Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia, issued on a recurring quarterly cycle. Not journalism-specific, but media and journalism projects are an eligible category.
grants.notes: General regional-cooperation fund, not exclusively for media/journalism; included because GFMD lists it as a journalism-relevant funding opportunity.

grants.summary: Supports U.S.-based reporting on Missing and Murdered Indigenous People/Women, Girls, Two-Spirit and Transgender people (MMIP/WG2T). Open to Indigenous and non-Indigenous journalists affiliated with media outlets as well as freelancers, with applications accepted on a rolling basis.
grants.notes: Also provides editorial and pitching support to grantees in addition to funding; new entry, not previously in the dataset.

grants.programme: Reproductive Health, Rights and Justice in the Americas
grants.summary: Reporting grants for women and nonbinary journalists covering reproductive health, rights and justice in Latin America, the Caribbean and the United States, open to individual or team applications. The 2026 cycle is open; preference is given to multimedia teams focused on Argentina, Brazil and Chile, or on transnational right-wing-network reporting.
grants.notes: Open to women and nonbinary journalists only; deadline not found. This programme's own IWMF subpage was not among the pages captured in today's snapshot. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Journalismfund Europe's oldest grant programme, supporting investigative journalism in Dutch-language media in Belgium since 1999. It is subsidised by the Flemish Government and funds both experienced and young journalists' investigative projects.

amount.note: €270,000 available in 2026 across 4 application rounds (approx. €67,500 per round); individual grant amount not stated.

grants.notes: Fourth and final 2026 round (previous rounds: 22 Jan, 23 Apr, 6 Aug 2026).

grants.summary: Supports cross-border teams of professional journalists and/or news outlets investigating original, in-depth stories relevant to European audiences, running since 2009. Teams can also work with project advisors and subject-matter experts through the programme's expert-reviewed journalism component.

amount.note: Individual grant amount not stated on the funder's page.

grants.notes: Requires a cross-border team (journalists and/or outlets from different countries); solo national applications are not the intended format of this grant. Also appears on the GFMD funding aggregator (which listed a 15 Oct 2026 deadline for what is likely the same round); the funder's own page today states 1 Oct 2026, which takes precedence here.

grants.summary: Supports collaborative investigative projects led by Dutch-speaking and French-speaking Belgian journalists working together on local issues with national relevance. Teams must include at least one journalist from each language community and publish in at least two Belgian outlets, one French and one Dutch.

amount.note: €50,000 total available per call across all funded investigations; individual grant amount not stated.

grants.notes: Applicants must be legally resident in Belgium; supported by the King Baudouin Foundation. Eligibility and amount details found via web search, not stated on the captured snapshot. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Supports cross-border teams of professional journalists and/or news outlets investigating the welfare and living conditions of farmed animals within European food systems, including related regulation, supply chains and environmental pressures. Teams also receive mentor support alongside funding.

amount.note: €150,000 available per call (€300,000 total for 2026); individual grant amount not stated.

grants.notes: Topic focus and amount confirmed via web search; the snapshot's description of this programme was truncated before those details. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Reporting grants funding in-depth journalism on the development, deployment, and societal impact of artificial intelligence systems. Awarded on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline, open to freelance and staff journalists worldwide via the Center's general grant application.
grants.notes: Confirmed as a currently listed programme on the Center's Grants & Fellowships navigation. Supersedes the previously tracked 'AI Accountability Fellowships (2026-27)', which no longer appears anywhere on the funder's site. Theme-specific amount/eligibility not detailed on captured pages. grants.notes: Confirmed as a currently listed programme on the Center's Grants & Fellowships navigation. Theme-specific amount/eligibility not detailed on captured pages. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: Confirmed as a currently listed programme on the Center's Grants & Fellowships navigation. Theme-specific amount/eligibility not detailed on captured pages. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: Confirmed as a currently listed programme on the Center's Grants & Fellowships navigation. Theme-specific amount/eligibility not detailed on captured pages. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: geoScope reflects the region of reporting focus, not a restriction on applicant nationality (the Center states it accepts freelance and staff journalists worldwide). Theme-specific amount/eligibility not detailed on captured pages. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Reporting grants supporting local news journalism within the United States, part of the Center's U.S. Local News Reporting initiative. Awarded on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline via the Center's general grant application.
grants.notes: Confirmed as a currently listed programme on the Center's Grants & Fellowships navigation, tied to the U.S. Local News Reporting initiative. Theme-specific amount/eligibility not detailed on captured pages. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: Confirmed as a currently listed programme on the Center's Grants & Fellowships navigation. Theme-specific amount/eligibility not detailed on captured pages. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Media Innovation Europe: Audience-Engaged Journalism Grants
grants.summary: Grants for media outlets from six Western Balkan and four Visegrad countries to produce audience-engaged journalism, with access to BIRN's BE-Engaged digital tool plus training, technical assistance and editorial mentoring. Also listed on the GFMD funding aggregator under a shorter title; consolidated here as it comes from BIRN's own site, one of the scheme's administering partners. Deadline and per-grant cap found via web search since today's snapshot described the wider project but not this specific call's deadline in detail. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A Horizon Europe Cluster 2 call funding consortium projects that reinforce the digital transformation of news media through new business models and audience engagement approaches. Requires a consortium of at least three independent legal entities in different countries, including at least one news media organisation.

amount.note: Estimated EU contribution per project; total call budget €12,000,000 across all funded projects.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of the EU Funding & Tenders Portal captured an unrelated generic topic-code list, not this call's page, so all details here come from web search. Requires a multi-country consortium; not something a single freelancer or newsroom can apply for alone. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Identifying user-focused solutions to support news media freedom (HORIZON-CL2-2027-01-DEMOCRACY-06)
grants.summary: A Horizon Europe Cluster 2 call funding research into news consumption patterns and tools to help news media organisations and journalists adapt to digital transformation and reach new audiences. Up to three projects will be funded, each requiring a multi-country consortium including news media organisations.

amount.note: Estimated EU contribution per project for up to 3 projects.

grants.notes: Part of the Horizon Europe 2026-2027 work programme; exact call opening date not confirmed, so status is set to upcoming rather than open. Today's snapshot did not contain this call — details from web search. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A free, 24/7 rapid-response service providing real-time technical assistance and cybersecurity advice to civil society groups, activists, media organisations, journalists, bloggers, and human rights defenders facing digital threats. amount.note: Provides technical assistance, not a cash grant.

grants.notes: Today's accessnow.org snapshot covered the general 'Access Now Grants' grassroots-grantmaking page and a donor financial log, neither of which detailed the Helpline; details confirmed via web search of the funder's /help/ page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: ARIJ — Arab Reporters for Investigative Journalism
grants.summary: ARIJ awards grants of US$2,500 to Arab journalists to produce digital, audio, or televised investigative reports exposing environmental, legal, and financial corruption, separately covering filming and editing expenses. ARIJ's own site nav invites ongoing submission of investigation proposals alongside editorial mentoring and fact-checking support.

amount.note: US$2,500 per investigative report grant; ARIJ separately covers filming/video-editing expenses.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of arij.net confirms a standing 'Submit an investigation' (قدم تحقيقاً) intake and references pausing responses over winter holidays, indicating an ongoing/rolling submission process, but did not capture ARIJ's dedicated grants page. The $2,500 amount and eligible-country list come from a search of ARIJ's own site (en.arij.net) rather than today's snapshot content. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A year-long, non-residential fellowship for activists, investigative journalists, filmmakers and lawyers to collaboratively investigate one pressing social-justice issue chosen around an annual theme. Reported support has included a fellow stipend, project funding, and a 'connect fund' for collaboration, plus training, mentorship and networking.

amount.note: Previously reported (secondary sources, prior cycle): fellow stipend up to US$64,900, project funding up to US$10,000, and a connect fund up to US$5,000.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot confirms the programme exists ('Fellowships for Activists, Investigative Journalists, Filmmakers and Lawyers to spend a year working on one pressing social justice challenge') and states verbatim: BERTHA FOUNDATION DOES NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS — applications are only taken during announced windows. The most recent verified deadline (28 Jul 2025, for a fellowship year beginning Jan 2026) has passed; no 2026/2027 call was found open today. Programme appears to recur roughly annually. Not confirmed on the funder's own page for deadline/amount specifics.

grants.summary: Travel fellowships for journalists, journalism students and early-career science communicators to attend the World Conference of Science Journalists 2027 in London (6-9 September 2027), covering travel, visa costs, limited local transport, up to six nights' accommodation and conference registration. Selection weighs professional merit, motivation, and financial need.

amount.note: Covers travel, visa costs, limited local transport and up to six nights' accommodation, plus conference registration; no fixed cash amount stated.

grants.notes: GIJN's Grants & Fellowships aggregator page failed to fetch today (HTTP 403); found via web search referencing GIJN's listing and corroborated on the fellowship's own official registration site. Also independently surfaced via the GFMD aggregator; consolidated here since this version has a confirmed official application URL. Not confirmed on the funder's own page (GIJN's).

grants.summary: Astraea's International Fund gives flexible, core support to grassroots LGBTQI-led groups outside the US and Canada, across Africa, Asia/the Pacific, Eastern Europe/the former Soviet space, Latin America/the Caribbean and the Middle East. Grants back a group's own agenda rather than a single deliverable, and the foundation names media-making and storytelling among what it wants LGBTQI groups equipped to do.
grants.eligibleActivity: Astraea states its commitment is to 'equip [LGBTQI activists] with the tools to make their own media and control their own narratives,' so a media, storytelling or documentation project can be funded as core organisational work — but only for a grantee that is itself LGBTQI-led (Astraea explicitly does not fund groups without LGBTQI leadership), not for a general newsroom or freelancer applying on journalistic grounds alone. A freelance journalist would need to apply through, or as part of, a qualifying LGBTQI-led organisation.

amount.note: Applicant organisations must have an annual budget under USD 500,000; no specific per-grant ceiling was found stated.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of astraeafoundation.org/grants/ was only a 145-word cookie-consent shell with no grant content (likely JS-rendered), so this entry relies entirely on WebSearch. The International Fund excludes the US and Canada and covers Africa, Asia/Pacific, Eastern Europe/former-Soviet countries, Latin America/Caribbean and the Middle East; whether Serbia specifically falls in Astraea's 'Eastern Europe' grouping was not confirmed, so geoScope is left as global rather than guessed. No specific 2026 deadline or grant-size ceiling was found; treat as an LOI-based rolling fund pending direct confirmation. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: EU Delegation to Serbia (via "Glas(no) o pravima" project)
grants.programme: Glas(no) o pravima: EU Grantovi za organizacije i medije
grants.summary: An EU-funded call offering EUR 12,000 per project to civil society organisations and independent media in Serbia to improve how human rights are communicated to and understood by local communities. It responds to research showing a gap between how CSOs talk about human rights and how citizens actually understand them.
grants.eligibleActivity: The call's own eligibility line names 'organizacije civilnog društva i nezavisne medije' (civil society organisations AND independent media) as who may apply, so a media outlet applies directly rather than through an inferred route. Its stated aim — supporting projects that improve how human rights are communicated and understood in local communities — is squarely a reporting/public-education activity, not a generic civil-society grant repurposed for journalism.

amount.note: 12.000 evra po projektu, per today's snapshot of the call page.

grants.programme: Direct Aid Program (DAP) — Serbia, North Macedonia & Montenegro
grants.summary: Australia's small-grants aid programme, managed by the Embassy in Belgrade, funds small-scale community and civil-society projects in Serbia, North Macedonia and Montenegro. It runs as an annual call — most recently open 15 September to 5 October 2025 — and the exact FY2026-27 opening/closing dates for the Belgrade round could not be confirmed today.
grants.eligibleActivity: DAP's own published priorities for Serbia/North Macedonia/Montenegro explicitly list 'promoting human rights, media freedom and good governance' alongside gender equality and youth priorities, so a documentation, reporting or public-education project on human rights, corruption or press-freedom issues sits under a named priority, not an inferred one. Funding is awarded to the project rather than to the applicant's profession, so an outlet would need to apply as, or in partnership with, a registered local NGO/CSO in Serbia, North Macedonia or Montenegro rather than as an individual freelancer.

amount.note: Up to €10,000 for a single project.

grants.notes: The embassy's own page states: "Australian Direct Aid Program 2026-27… This round will be opened from 8 September to 4 October 2026", a €10,000 ceiling per project, and projects running between 1 December 2026 and 31 December 2027.

amount.note: Up to €10,000 for a single project.

pinned.notes: The embassy's own page states: "Australian Direct Aid Program 2026-27… This round will be opened from 8 September to 4 October 2026", a €10,000 ceiling per project, and projects running between 1 December 2026 and 31 December 2027.
pinned._why: Read directly on serbia.embassy.gov.au on 17 and 18 September 2026. The sweep cannot see this: the DAP portal does not render as text, so it falls back to search, which returns the closed FY2025-26 round (AUD 20,000, October 2025) and reports the current round as unknown. Pinned until the portal becomes readable.

grants.programme: Media Training & Development (MT&D) Small Grants Program
grants.summary: A recurring small-grants line run by the U.S. Embassy Belgrade's Public Diplomacy Section, aimed specifically at strengthening the Serbian press and the free flow of accurate information. Past rounds (2020 and a 2024 round focused on countering foreign information manipulation and interference) funded workshops, training courses, conferences, hackathons and online projects; only registered organisations may apply, not individuals.
grants.eligibleActivity: This is not an inferred fit: the funder's own stated purpose for this specific small-grants line is 'to fund individual projects that support the strengthening of the Serbian press and ensure the free flow of accurate information to keep Serbia's citizens informed.' The most recent (2024) round required proposals to counter foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI); applications may only come from organisations, not individual freelance journalists.

amount.note: No award ceiling found in the sources checked; historic notices did not disclose a per-project cap.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot fetch for this source failed, so this entry is built entirely from WebSearch: a 2020 embassy announcement and a 2024 Notice of Funding Opportunity (focused on countering FIMI) describe a recurring MT&D small-grants line, organisations only, but no current 2026 round or deadline could be found. Check rs.usembassy.gov/grants-programs-2/ directly for the live status. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: European Union (NDICI-Global Europe, via EU Delegations worldwide)
grants.programme: Thematic Programme on Human Rights and Democracy (successor to EIDHR)
grants.summary: The EU's flagship global human-rights and democracy funding instrument under NDICI-Global Europe (2021-2027). Rather than one fixed call, it operates as a rolling, multi-country programme: individual EU Delegations publish their own periodic calls for proposals for local civil-society organisations, each with its own budget, country scope and deadline.
grants.eligibleActivity: The programme's own Multiannual Indicative Programme (2021-2027) names 'freedom of expression, supporting independent journalism and media' and 'inclusive and sustainable support measures for journalists, especially women journalists, and whistle-blowers' as an explicit strand of its Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms priority — so investigative reporting, media-support or journalist-protection projects sit under a named priority, not an inferred one. Grants go to registered non-profit CSOs (or public-sector/local-authority partners) under individual country/regional calls, not to individual freelance journalists directly.

amount.note: No global award ceiling found; amounts vary by the individual country/regional call published under this thematic programme.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of the EU International Partnerships landing page (~1290 words, mostly repeated across language variants) was navigation/boilerplate only — the priority language on independent journalism/media support was not visible there and comes from the programme's Multiannual Indicative Programme, found via WebSearch. Individual country calls (e.g. a West Bank/Gaza round with a 26 Jan 2026 concept-note deadline, already passed) open and close on a rolling basis via EU Delegations and the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, not on this landing page itself, so no single current deadline could be confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: The Gene Roberts Fund for Emergency Assistance
grants.summary: CPJ provides case-by-case emergency financial support to journalists who have recently faced a serious incident and whose safety is compromised, through the Gene Roberts Fund, administered by CPJ staff in New York and overseen by a board committee. Funds may cover relocation expenses, medical costs, mental health support, legal help and other urgent needs; CPJ cannot fund visa or immigration/asylum applications, education, or general medical needs unrelated to an act of journalism. CPJ separately offers non-financial assistance such as referrals to partner organisations, fellowship/residency information, and safety or trauma consultations.

amount.note: Described only as 'modest grants' assessed case by case; no fixed amount stated on CPJ's own pages.

grants.notes: CPJ explicitly excludes visa applications, immigration/asylum claims, education costs, and general medical needs unrelated to an act of journalism from this fund's scope.

grants.summary: Craig Newmark Philanthropies accepts funding proposals from registered nonprofits on a rolling basis across its focus areas, one of which is 'Promoting the Truth'; a separate portal exists only for veterans/military-family support. Applicants must supply proof of active 501(c)(3)/public-charity status with the IRS and Secretary of State, and CNP says it cannot review or fund every request. Multi-year commitments are released annually based on progress and the effectiveness of the grantee's communication and collaboration.

amount.note: Application asks for a 'grant amount requested' but no published range.

grants.notes: Reporting from January 2026 (Nieman Journalism Lab) quotes founder Craig Newmark saying he is pulling back from journalism funding because 'a lot of my efforts haven't been as effective as I'd like them to be,' now treating journalism as a secondary focus behind cybersecurity and safety of journalists — so openness to new 'Promoting the Truth' proposals from newsrooms may be more limited than the site's generic apply page suggests. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Media Defence provides legal grants and practical support for the defence of journalists, citizen journalists and media outlets facing prosecution or civil suits connected to their work. Applications for case support are usually made by the lawyer handling the case but can also be made by the journalist, their family or friends, or a relevant support organisation. Media Defence combines financial assistance with practical support to organisations that have, or wish to establish, a legal aid unit for journalists.

amount.note: Covers legal costs case-by-case; no published amount range found.

grants.notes: No snapshot was available for mediadefence.org (fetch never produced a file), so this entry is built from web search of the funder's own site pages (apply-for-case-support/, get-help/). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Partner support for legal aid organisations
grants.summary: Media Defence funds and supports partner organisations that operate, or want to establish, a legal aid unit providing free legal support to journalists, citizen journalists and media outlets facing legal threats. In 2025 it reported awarding over £350,000 in grants to 19 partner organisations running media-defence centres across Europe, Latin America, Africa, Asia, and the Middle East/North Africa, enabling litigation of hundreds of freedom-of-expression cases.

amount.note: £350,000+ distributed across 19 partner organisations in 2025 in aggregate; no per-grant figure published.

grants.notes: No snapshot was available for mediadefence.org; this entry (distinct from individual case support) is built from web search covering the funder's own 'get-help' page and a 2025 partner impact report. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: RSF's Assistance Desk provides financial and administrative help to professional and citizen journalists who have been the target of reprisals connected to their reporting, covering emergency relocation, legal fees, medical costs, psychological support and replacement of destroyed or confiscated equipment. Grants generally range from EUR 500 to EUR 2,500 per case, and RSF may also support applications for international protection or asylum where its research supports it. In 2025 RSF reported aiding nearly 750 journalists in 76 countries.

amount.note: Per-case emergency support grant range reported by RSF; larger relocation/asylum cases may exceed this via other mechanisms.

grants.notes: No snapshot was available for rsf.org/en/assistance; amount range and scope are drawn from web search of RSF's own reporting and individual-support page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: RSF launched a grant programme reimbursing US-based journalists for personal protective equipment, including first-aid kits, helmets, eye protection, protective vests and respirator masks, in response to escalating on-the-ground risks to reporters covering protests and conflict.

amount.note: Reimbursement scheme; no published cap found.

grants.notes: No snapshot was available for this source; found via web search of RSF's own news release announcing the US-specific PRESS equipment grant programme. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Balkan Trust for Democracy (German Marshall Fund)
grants.programme: BTD Support for Western Balkans 6 — Media Freedom track
grants.summary: The Balkan Trust for Democracy funds civil society organisations registered in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. One of its two current thematic tracks is strengthening media freedom (the other combats domestic and gender-based violence), delivered as a sub-granting scheme realised with the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Royal Norwegian Embassy in Belgrade. Proposals have previously been accepted on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline until the grantmaking budget is exhausted.
grants.notes: Re-checked on 2026-09-18: today's snapshot of gmfus.org again only captured generic GMF organisational pages (About, Global Power Shifts, Fellowships, donor FAQ, a press article) and never reached Balkan Trust for Democracy's own grant-call pages, so this entry is still built from a web search of GMF's own site (balkan-trust-democracy/support-western-balkans-6 and the related WB6 media-freedom announcement page confirm the six-country scope and Norwegian co-funding). Only registered civil-society organisations in the six WB6 countries may apply — not individual freelancers. No corroborated deadline was found; secondary sites reference other, separate WB6 media programmes (e.g. EU/EEAS 'WB6 MEDIA') with their own deadlines that should not be conflated with this BTD call. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Emergency response fund providing direct assistance, legal support and safety advice to journalists, fixers and media outlets in distress worldwide who face (online) harassment, intimidation, legal proceedings or violence because of their work. The emergency must be a direct result of the applicant's journalism work and be confirmed by at least two trusted sources outside the applicant.

amount.note: Assessed case by case; typical response time cited as 48-72 hours, with faster turnaround (up to 24 hours) for the most urgent cases.

grants.notes: Replaces prior unverified seed entry. Application form accepts submissions in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese; contact reportersrespond@freepressunlimited.org. No snapshot of the funder's page was available this run, so this is based on web search results only. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Healthy Information Sphere (International Human Rights Programme)
grants.summary: Oak Foundation's Healthy Information Sphere portfolio, within its International Human Rights Programme, supports independent journalism, media pluralism, digital rights and information integrity work aimed at holding power to account. Not-for-profit organisations not already invited by a programme officer may submit an unsolicited Letter of Enquiry, though the Foundation states it has no open call for proposals and funds only a small share of the enquiries it receives.

amount.note: Not stated publicly; programme budgets are reported to be allocated roughly a year in advance and only a small number of unsolicited enquiries are funded each year.

grants.notes: This is a general unsolicited-Letter-of-Enquiry intake, not a journalism-specific open call; the Foundation explicitly says it has no open call for proposals at this time and only responds to enquiries submitted via its online form. Geographic focus reported as EU, US, UK, Brazil and other 'global East' geographies, so global scope is uncertain. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: MDIF provides loans, equity investments, loan guarantees and related business advisory support to independent media and information businesses operating in countries with a history of media oppression, ownership concentration, a state of democratic transition, or information poverty. This is investment capital rather than grant funding; applicants must be independent of government or other interest groups, complete an inquiry form, and go through a multi-step due-diligence process that typically takes several months.

amount.note: Case by case; specific loan/equity size ranges not stated publicly. MDIF reports a portfolio of roughly $118.7M across around 58-60 media businesses in 31-34 countries as of its most recent reporting found.

grants.notes: Replaces prior unverified seed entry. Not a grant — financing carries repayment (debt) or ownership (equity) terms. No snapshot of the funder's page was available this run, so this is based on web search results only. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: GNI Lab is a 12-week program combining virtual sessions, practical exercises and personalized mentoring that helps independent news creators and small digital media outlets strengthen their journalism using Google tools, audience-building practices, and revenue-diversification strategies. It is run by SembraMedia in partnership with the Google News Initiative for participants from Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru and Uruguay. The 2026 cohort's application window closed on August 2, 2026.

amount.note: Training and mentoring program; no cash grant amount was stated in search results.

grants.notes: The 2026 cohort's application window closed August 2, 2026 (Argentina time). SembraMedia runs this as a recurring initiative, so a future cycle is likely, but no confirmed next call date was found in search results. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: PULSE, n-ost's cross-border journalism network ('Europe beyond the beat'), funds small reporting teams of two journalists from different eligible countries to produce collaborative stories under one of four Thematic Networks (media and society, media/AI legislation, digitalisation, and disinformation/fact-checking). The 2026 call was open to journalists with fiscal residency across a broad list of countries including EU and EU-candidate states, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Brazil, China, India, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Russia, the UK, the US, Uzbekistan, Belarus, Israel/Palestine and Iran, with two teams funded per network. The pitch deadline was extended to July 20, 2026, with results expected in September 2026, so this cycle is now closed to new applicants.

amount.note: Grant amount per team was not stated in search results.

grants.notes: The 2026 Thematic Network pitch deadline (extended to July 20, 2026) has passed and results were due in September 2026. PULSE runs as a recurring annual programme, so a future call is expected, but no next date was found. The 2026 call's eligible journalist countries extend well beyond Europe (e.g. Brazil, China, India, US) even though the programme is Europe-focused; geoScope here reflects the programme's Europe focus, not the full eligibility list. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.
